statement: The Danelaw — the Norse-ruled territory of northern and eastern England established by the Great Heathen Army's settlement (865–878) — coexisted and competed with Wessex for nearly a century before the reconquest. The Danelaw was not a unified political entity but a patchwork of Danish-held towns (the Five Boroughs: Leicester, Nottingham, Derby, Stamford, Lincoln) and Norse-speaking rural areas. Alfred the Great's Treaty of Wedmore (878) established the boundary; his descendants — Edward the Elder (913–920) and Æthelflæd — reconquered it systematically, with the death of Eric Bloodaxe in 954 ending Norse Jorvik.
